[[File:Nododo_statues.png|thumb|250px|The four golden statues]]
Four '''sacred statues''' were hidden in the [[Gungan Caves]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. They held religious importance to the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]], a people of aquatic [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]].

==Description==
The [[Gold/Legends|golden]] statues were in the shape of an [[Opee sea killer/Legends|opee sea killer]], a [[Kaadu/Legends|kaadu]], a [[Peko-peko/Legends|peko-peko]], and a [[Shaak/Legends|shaak]]&mdash;four animals worshipped by the native [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]]. Each of them was kept behind a sealed door which would only open with the combination of ten jewel keys.<ref name="YCAC">''[[Star Wars: Yoda's Challenge Activity Center]]''</ref>

==History==
Sometime after [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}}</ref> [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] sent a [[Unidentified young new recruit|young Jedi recruit]] on a mission to recover the statues. With the help the jewel keys he had found in the cave system, the youngling successfully unlocked the doors protecting the statues.<ref name="YCAC" />

==Behind the scenes==
According to [[Daniel Wallace]], the cancelled book ''[[The Essential Guide to Episode I]]'' was to explain the origin of the statues. One of its entry would have explained that the Gungan trickster god Nododo could "only appear in physical form as an opee sea killer, a kaadu, a peko peko, or a shaak." This would have conformed to the tenets of Gungan pantheism.<ref name="LW EGEI notes">{{Blog|danwallace|34|Lostwords: The Essential Guide to Episode I}}</ref>
